match.reason: The closest bank point, The nuclear arms race, is broader and covers the arms race as a whole, with the 1962 crisis as only one part, so it does not teach the Cuban Missile Crisis itself at the depth this point needs.

draft.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
card: In 1962 the United States found that the Soviet Union was placing nuclear missiles in Cuba, an island close to the American coast.
President John F. Kennedy ordered a naval blockade of Cuba to stop more weapons arriving. He demanded that the missiles be removed.
For about two weeks the world feared nuclear war. Both leaders faced pressure to act, and a mistake could have led to a direct clash.
The crisis ended when Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles. The United States promised not to invade Cuba, and it also agreed privately to remove its missiles from Turkey.
draft.remember: Both sides stepped back from the brink: missiles left Cuba in return for promises.

a.q: How did Kennedy first respond to the missiles in Cuba?
opts: He ordered a naval blockade of Cuba
He ordered a nuclear strike on Cuba
He asked the Soviet Union to build more missiles
He invaded Cuba with American troops
a.why: Kennedy chose a blockade to stop more weapons arriving while talks continued. Invasion or a strike would have risked war, so it was not his first response.
a.clue: It was a way to stop ships without firing the first shot.

b.q: Why is the end of the crisis seen as both sides stepping back?
opts: Each side gave something up: missiles left Cuba and Turkey
Only the Soviet Union gave up anything, and it lost
Only the United States gave up anything, and it lost
Neither side gave up anything, as the crisis simply faded
b.why: The Soviet Union removed its missiles from Cuba, and the United States promised not to invade and agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey. Each side gave up something, so it was not a one-sided loss.
b.clue: Count what each side agreed to do.

a.best: He ordered a naval blockade of Cuba

b.best: Each side gave something up: missiles left Cuba and Turkey

problems.detail: The stem already says 'both sides stepping back', so the two 'Only one side gave up anything' options plainly contradict the question. The right option, 'Each side gave something up', echoes 'both sides' and is the only one with a precise detail (Turkey). A student could pick it without knowing the terms of the deal.

proposal.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
card: In 1962 the United States found that the Soviet Union was placing nuclear missiles in Cuba, an island close to the American coast.
President John F. Kennedy ordered a naval blockade of Cuba to stop more weapons arriving. He demanded that the missiles be removed.
For about two weeks the world feared nuclear war. Both leaders faced pressure to act, and a mistake could have led to a direct clash.

The crisis ended when Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles. The United States publicly promised not to invade Cuba, and it also agreed privately to remove its missiles from Turkey.
proposal.remember: Both sides stepped back from the brink: missiles left Cuba in return for promises.

a.q: How did Kennedy first respond to the missiles in Cuba?
opts: He ordered a naval blockade of Cuba
He ordered air strikes on the missile sites
He sent American troops to invade Cuba
He took US missiles out of Turkey at once
a.why: Kennedy chose a blockade to stop more weapons arriving while he demanded the missiles be removed. Removing missiles from Turkey came later, as part of the deal that ended the crisis, not as his first step.
a.clue: It was a way to stop ships without firing the first shot.

b.q: At the end of the crisis, which part of the deal was agreed privately rather than in public?
opts: US missiles would be taken out of Turkey
The US would not invade Cuba in the future
Soviet missiles would be taken out of Cuba
US ships would stop more weapons reaching Cuba
b.why: The United States agreed privately to remove its missiles from Turkey. The promise not to invade Cuba is tempting because it was also part of the deal, but it was made publicly.
b.clue: One promise by the United States was kept out of public view.

a.best: He ordered a naval blockade of Cuba

b.best: US missiles would be taken out of Turkey
